### Main

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Modern_Family&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Main")]

*   [Ed O'Neill](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ed_O'Neill "Ed O'Neill") as **Jay Francis Pritchett**: The wealthy patriarch of the family; husband of Gloria; father of Claire, Mitchell, and Joe; and stepfather of Manny. He is the founder and CEO of Pritchett's Closets & Blinds. After retiring, he later starts a dog bed business, Dog Beds by Stella.
*   [Sofía Vergara](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sof%C3%ADa_Vergara "Sofía Vergara") as **Gloria María Pritchett (née Ramírez)**: Jay's second wife; mother of Manny (with her first husband Javier) and Joe (with Jay). Originally from Colombia, she is passionate, outspoken, and family-oriented. She later launches a hot sauce business based on a family recipe. Even later, she becomes a realtor under Phil's mentorship.
*   [Julie Bowen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Julie_Bowen "Julie Bowen") as **Claire Melinda Dunphy (née Pritchett)**: Jay and Dede's daughter; Mitchell's sister; Phil's wife; and mother of Haley, Alex, and Luke. She is organized and high-strung. She succeeds Jay as CEO of Pritchett's Closets & Blinds before eventually stepping down.
*   [Ty Burrell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ty_Burrell "Ty Burrell") as **Philip Humphrey "Phil" Dunphy**: Claire's husband and father of Haley, Alex, and Luke. A real estate agent known for his enthusiastic personality, he later becomes a real estate professor. He is also an amateur magician and briefly owns a magic shop.
*   [Jesse Tyler Ferguson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jesse_Tyler_Ferguson "Jesse Tyler Ferguson") as **Mitchell Vincent Pritchett**: Jay and Dede's son; Claire's brother; Cameron's husband; and adoptive father of Lily and Rexford. He works as a lawyer, primarily in environmental law, and later becomes a prosecutor.
*   [Eric Stonestreet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eric_Stonestreet "Eric Stonestreet") as **Cameron Scott Tucker**: Mitchell's husband and adoptive father of Lily and Rexford. A former clown and music teacher, he later becomes a physical education teacher, football coach, and eventually vice principal.
*   [Sarah Hyland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sarah_Hyland "Sarah Hyland") as **Haley Gwendolyn Dunphy**: Claire and Phil's eldest daughter; sister of Alex and Luke; wife of Dylan; and mother of twins Poppy and George. Initially portrayed as a stereotypical "party girl," she later pursues a career in fashion and works at NERP, a lifestyle company.
*   [Ariel Winter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ariel_Winter "Ariel Winter") as **Alexandria Anastasia "Alex" Dunphy**: Claire and Phil's middle child; sister of Haley and Luke. ## Production

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Modern_Family&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: Production")]

### Initial development

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Modern_Family&action=edit&section=7 "Edit section: Initial development")]

As creators [Christopher Lloyd](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christopher_Lloyd_(TV_producer) "Christopher Lloyd (TV producer)") and [Steven Levitan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steven_Levitan "Steven Levitan") retold stories about their families, they realized that the stories could be the basis for a show. They started working on the idea of a family being observed in a mockumentary-style show.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Modern_Family#cite_note-25) They later decided that it could be a show about three families and their experiences.[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Modern_Family#cite_note-26) It was originally called _My American Family_,[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Modern_Family#cite_note-title-27) and the camera crew was originally supposed to have been run by a fictitious Dutch filmmaker named Geert Floortje, who had lived as a teenaged exchange student with the Pritchetts and had developed a crush on Claire (while Mitchell had developed a crush on him). The producers later felt that this component was unnecessary, and it was scrapped. Lloyd preferred to look at the show as "a family show done documentary-style".[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Modern_Family#cite_note-28)

Lloyd and Levitan [pitched](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pitch_(filmmaking) "Pitch (filmmaking)") the series to [CBS](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CBS "CBS"), [NBC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NBC "NBC"), and ABC (they did not pitch it to [Fox](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fox_Broadcasting_Company "Fox Broadcasting Company") because of issues they had with the network over a previous comedy series, _[Back to You](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Back\_to\_You\_(TV\_series) "Back to You (TV series)")_, that Lloyd and Levitan also created and produced). CBS, which was not ready to make a big commitment to the single-camera style of filming, rejected the series. NBC, already broadcasting _[The Office](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Office\_(American\_TV\_series) "The Office (American TV series)")_ and _[Parks and Recreation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Parks\_and\_Recreation "Parks and Recreation")_ at the time, decided against taking on a third mockumentary-style show. ABC accepted the pitch.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Modern_Family#cite_note-29)

The [pilot](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Television_pilot "Television pilot") episode tested positively with [focus groups](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Focus_group "Focus group"), resulting in the network ordering 13 episodes and adding it to the [2009–10 fall lineup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2009%E2%80%9310_United_States_network_television_schedule "2009–10 United States network television schedule") days ahead of ABC's official schedule announcement.[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Modern_Family#cite_note-OrderedToSeries-30) The series was given a full-season pickup in October 2009.[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Modern_Family#cite_note-FullSeasonPickup-31)

### Filming

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Modern_Family&action=edit&section=8 "Edit section: Filming")]

[Principal photography](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Principal_photography "Principal photography") took place in Los Angeles.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Modern_Family#cite_note-Variety_review-32) Many of the exteriors used are on the city's [Westside](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Westside_(Los_Angeles_County) "Westside (Los Angeles County)"). The Dunphys' house is in the [Cheviot Hills](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cheviot_Hills,_Los_Angeles "Cheviot Hills, Los Angeles") neighborhood. As of 2014[[update]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Modern_Family&action=edit), [Palisades Charter High School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palisades_Charter_High_School "Palisades Charter High School") is used for the exteriors of Luke and Manny's school.[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Modern_Family#cite_note-Slate_west_LA_article-33)

Lloyd and Levitan, whose credits both include _[Frasier](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Frasier "Frasier")_, _[Wings](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wings\_(1990\_TV\_series) "Wings (1990 TV series)")_, and _[Just Shoot Me!](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Just\_Shoot\_Me! "Just Shoot Me!")_, are executive producers of the series, serving as [showrunner](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Showrunner "Showrunner") and [head writer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Head_writer "Head writer") under their Lloyd-Levitan Productions label in affiliation with [20th Century Fox Television](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/20th_Century_Fox_Television "20th Century Fox Television").[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Modern_Family#cite_note-Variety_review-32) The other original producers on the writing team were Paul Corrigan, [Sameer Gardezi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sameer_Asad_Gardezi "Sameer Asad Gardezi"), [Joe Lawson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Lawson_(writer) "Joe Lawson (writer)"), [Dan O'Shannon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dan_O'Shannon "Dan O'Shannon"), Brad Walsh, Caroline Williams, Bill Wrubel, Danny Zuker, and Jeff Morton.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Modern_Family#cite_note-Variety_review-32)[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Modern_Family#cite_note-34)

Starting with the second season, Lloyd and Levitan ran the show, not as a team, but separately, with each showrunner supervising half the episodes. "Chris and I are both strong, opinionated people, and we very, very quickly realized it doesn't make sense to sit here and debate each other and waste time," Levitan told _[The Hollywood Reporter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Hollywood\_Reporter "The Hollywood Reporter")_ in 2012. "We often come at it from different points of view, so we said, 'Let's just switch off who has final say.'"[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Modern_Family#cite_note-35)

### Litigation

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Modern_Family&action=edit&section=9 "Edit section: Litigation")]

[![Image 5](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/5/5f/Modern_Family_Cast.jpg/330px-Modern_Family_Cast.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Modern_Family_Cast.jpg)

Cast of _Modern Family_ at the [69th Golden Globe Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/69th_Golden_Globe_Awards "69th Golden Globe Awards") in January 2012

In the first season, the adult cast was paid a range of roughly $30,000 to $90,000 per episode.[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Modern_Family#cite_note-36) As a result of the show's success, the cast attempted to renegotiate their contracts in the summer of 2012 to obtain higher per-episode fees, but talks broke down to the point that the fourth season's first [table read](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Read-through "Read-through") had to be postponed.

Five of the cast members ([Ty Burrell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ty_Burrell "Ty Burrell"), [Julie Bowen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Julie_Bowen "Julie Bowen"), [Jesse Tyler Ferguson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jesse_Tyler_Ferguson "Jesse Tyler Ferguson"), [Eric Stonestreet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eric_Stonestreet "Eric Stonestreet") and [Sofía Vergara](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sof%C3%ADa_Vergara "Sofía Vergara")) retained the [Quinn Emanuel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quinn_Emanuel_Urquhart_&_Sullivan "Quinn Emanuel Urquhart & Sullivan") law firm and sued 20th Century Fox Television in [Los Angeles County Superior Court](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Los_Angeles_County_Superior_Court "Los Angeles County Superior Court") on July 24, 2012.[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Modern_Family#cite_note-docket-37) While not part of the lawsuit, [Ed O'Neill](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ed_O'Neill "Ed O'Neill") joined his fellow castmates in seeking raises for each to about $200,000 per episode; O'Neill had already been earning more money per episode than the other five. The lawsuit invoked the "seven-year rule" in California Labor Code Section 2855 (the [De Havilland Law](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/De_Havilland_Law "De Havilland Law")) and requested a [declaration](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Declaratory_judgment "Declaratory judgment") that their contracts were void because they were in violation of that rule.[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Modern_Family#cite_note-38)

By October 25, 2012, the conflict had been in final talks for a settlement, with plaintiffs planning thereafter to file a dismissal (which they ultimately did on November 19, 2012).[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Modern_Family#cite_note-docket-37) The five adult cast members' salaries were increased from $55,000–$65,000 per episode to $150,000–$175,000, with increases every season, plus a percentage of residual profits.[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Modern_Family#cite_note-39) O'Neill had already been earning $200,000 an episode, so his salary was lowered to parity with his co-stars, but with a larger percentage of the back-end profits.[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Modern_Family#cite_note-40) By that August, four of the five child stars negotiated increases from $15,000–$25,000 to $70,000 per episode,[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Modern_Family#cite_note-41) with an additional $10,000 per season raise.[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Modern_Family#cite_note-42)

## Themes and analysis

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Modern_Family&action=edit&section=11 "Edit section: Themes and analysis")]

### Technology and social media

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Modern_Family&action=edit&section=12 "Edit section: Technology and social media")]

In _[The New York Times](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_New\_York\_Times "The New York Times")_, [Bruce Feiler](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bruce_Feiler "Bruce Feiler") called attention to how the show depicts the increasing way communications technology shapes the way people perceive others, even family members. "[It] is surely the first family comedy that incorporates its own [hashtag](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hashtag "Hashtag") of simultaneous self-analysis directly into the storyline," he writes. "[Mark Zuckerberg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Zuckerberg "Mark Zuckerberg") may be a greater influence on _Modern Family_ than [Norman Lear](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Norman_Lear "Norman Lear")."[[54]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Modern_Family#cite_note-Feiler_NYT_piece-54)

The show's writers and actors agree. "We used to talk about how cellphones killed the sitcom because no one ever goes to anyone's house anymore" for routine information, [Abraham Higginbotham](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abraham_Higginbotham "Abraham Higginbotham") told Feiler. "We embrace technology so it's part of the story." Ty Burrell draws on [Fran Lebowitz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fran_Lebowitz "Fran Lebowitz")'s observation that there is no institution other than media.[[55]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Modern_Family#cite_note-55) "I had this little flash of Phil—and me—that we are parsing our personality together externally from how people perceive us."[[54]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Modern_Family#cite_note-Feiler_NYT_piece-54)

### Parenthood challenges and tradition

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Modern_Family&action=edit&section=13 "Edit section: Parenthood challenges and tradition")]

_Modern Family_ thoroughly explores the different parenting styles and challenges presented by modern circumstances and the unique personalities of children. James Parker of _[The Atlantic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Atlantic "The Atlantic")_ commented, "How does one 'parent'? Who does what, which 'role'? Is Dad sufficiently dad-like and Mom enough of a mom?"[[56]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Modern_Family#cite_note-parker-56) Throughout the show, Claire is a "daddy's girl" with a strong relationship with Jay, while Mitch has a much stronger bond with their mother. Jay struggles to connect with his step-son Manny initially, and often ridicules Manny's preferences for luxury and lack of masculine interests. However, Jay learns to accept and celebrate Manny's unique interests and skills in theater and film.

The gendered expectations of parenting are explored with Claire and Phil's family. Their relationship counters traditional male-dominated family structures by showing Claire as the family's decision maker while Phil is a 'fun dad'. Claire and Phil also deal with their three children's different personalities and life paths as individuals. They attempt to push Haley and Luke to pursue their education seriously and are met with resistance as the two children are more interested in other life paths. Specifically, Claire has a challenging relationship with Haley: Claire thinks she's helping direct Haley's school and career choices, while Haley thinks she's being too pushy and demanding, and will act out accordingly.[[57]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Modern_Family#cite_note-57) Ultimately, Claire learns to respect her eldest daughter's decisions regarding family and career, even though she does not necessarily approve of them.

### Queer family and parenting

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Modern_Family&action=edit&section=14 "Edit section: Queer family and parenting")]

One parenting challenge is explored with Jay's straining relationship with Mitchell due to his discomfort at having a gay son. This is explored in the season 5 episode "Message Received": gay marriage is legalized and Mitch and Cam decide to get married. Mitchell questions Jay's motives for not inviting his friends to his son's wedding by asking "So, who doesn't want them there, me or you?". Jay admits he doesn't understand gay marriages and blames Mitchell for not making him comfortable by saying "Now see, why do you get to be you, but I don't get to be me. See, I didn't choose to be uncomfortable. I was born this way." In response, Mitch un-invites his father to his wedding, but they later reconcile and Jay saves the wedding by hosting it at his country club and brags about the marriage to other club members.

_Modern Family_ is notable for its portrayal of queer and non-traditional family structures, primarily through the characters of Mitchell Pritchett and Cameron Tucker, a gay couple raising their adopted Vietnamese daughter, Lily. Their family dynamic was one of the first on prime-time television to center a same-sex couple navigating the challenges and rewards of parenthood, offering audiences an authentic look into LGBTQ+ family life. Throughout the series, Mitch and Cam's relationship showcases both the unique joys and social obstacles facing LGBTQ+ parents, such as dealing with stereotypes, facing subtle forms of prejudice, and navigating societal expectations. By depicting Mitch and Cam's journey as parents and partners in a relatable, humorous light, _Modern Family_ has played a significant role in normalizing LGBTQ+ families in mainstream media. The show's inclusion of various family forms, from blended families to adoptive and queer families, reflects a more inclusive view of what family means today and has been credited with increasing public acceptance of LGBTQ+ families. This representation contributes to broader conversations on family diversity, challenging traditional norms and encouraging viewers to embrace different family structures as equally valid and loving.[[58]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Modern_Family#cite_note-58)

### Masculinity and fatherhood

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Modern_Family&action=edit&section=15 "Edit section: Masculinity and fatherhood")]

The show has also been praised for portrayal of masculinity and fatherhood. In a 2016 review, journalist [Tim Dowling](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tim_Dowling "Tim Dowling") notes that "one of the main complaints voiced by so-called men's rights activists is that in popular culture husbands and fathers are routinely portrayed as moronic incompetents ... More sensible men's advocates, meanwhile, maintain that men are still straitjacketed by old expectations, and given no room to express vulnerability, doubt, or any emotion besides anger. Masculinity, it seems, just doesn't furnish the modern male with very many acceptable ways to be." While Dowling goes on to address the show's portrayal of Phil as the most "subversive" of the four fathers, the characters of Jay, Cam, and Mitchell also contribute to a mediated understanding of fatherhood that legitimizes a variety of "acceptable ways to be" a modern father. Through the vehicle of comedy, which exposes each of the characters' best and worst qualities, viewers can both witness and interrogate the qualities of the "traditional dad" and the "new dad", a distinction that emerges quite clearly as a new generation of men take the parenting reins from their own fathers.[[59]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Modern_Family#cite_note-59)

### Depiction of Los Angeles

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Modern_Family&action=edit&section=16 "Edit section: Depiction of Los Angeles")]

In a 2014 article in _[Slate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Slate\_(website) "Slate (website)")_, the site's podcast executive producer, Andy Bowers, a resident of Los Angeles' Westside, where the show films most of its exteriors, praised the series for its realistic depiction of life in that part of the city.[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Modern_Family#cite_note-Slate_west_LA_article-33)

## Release

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Modern_Family&action=edit&section=17 "Edit section: Release")]

### Broadcast

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Modern_Family&action=edit&section=18 "Edit section: Broadcast")]

_Modern Family_ was picked up for syndication by [USA Network](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USA_Network "USA Network") for $1.5 million per episode, along with being offered in local syndication at the same time, with [Fox Television Stations](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fox_Television_Stations "Fox Television Stations") the lead station group picking up the series.[[60]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Modern_Family#cite_note-mftousa-60)[[61]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Modern_Family#cite_note-mftousapress-61)[[62]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Modern_Family#cite_note-money-62) It is also shown on [Sky Comedy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sky_Comedy "Sky Comedy") and [E4](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/E4_(TV_channel) "E4 (TV channel)") in the [United Kingdom](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Kingdom "United Kingdom"), [e.tv](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/E.tv "E.tv") in [South Africa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Africa "South Africa"), Fox in [Sweden](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sweden "Sweden"), [yes Comedy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yes_Comedy "Yes Comedy") in [Israel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel "Israel") and [Star World](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Star_World_(Indian_TV_channel) "Star World (Indian TV channel)") in [India](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/India "India"). The series aired on [Citytv](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Citytv "Citytv") in [Canada](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Canada "Canada") for its first ten seasons.[[63]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Modern_Family#cite_note-63) The network additionally obtained the syndicated strip-rights to the show when they became available. Subsequently, it moved to [Global](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Global_Television_Network "Global Television Network") for its eleventh and final season.[[64]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Modern_Family#cite_note-64)_Modern Family_ moved to E! in Fall 2021 until September 6, 2024, and it began airing on [TBS](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/TBS_(American_TV_channel) "TBS (American TV channel)") since September 25, 2023, it was also aired on [TLC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/TLC_(TV_network) "TLC (TV network)") around August 2025, it was picked up by [Nickelodeon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nickelodeon "Nickelodeon") for its [Nick at Nite](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nick_at_Nite "Nick at Nite") block, starting on September 10, 2024 until it removed on August 31, 2026,[[65]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Modern_Family#cite_note-65)[[66]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Modern_Family#cite_note-66) and it was moved to [Freeform](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Freeform_(TV_channel) "Freeform (TV channel)") and [FX](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FX_(TV_channel) "FX (TV channel)") in October 2026. As of 2025, _Modern Family_ is streaming on Peacock and Hulu.[[67]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Modern_Family#cite_note-67)[[68]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Modern_Family#cite_note-68)

### Home media

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Modern_Family&action=edit&section=19 "Edit section: Home media")]

As of 2017, _Modern Family_ had earned $72,226,621 from its domestic home media releases.[[69]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Modern_Family#cite_note-69) The series was made available for streaming on [Hulu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hulu "Hulu") and [Peacock](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peacock_(streaming_service) "Peacock (streaming service)") in its entirety on February 3, 2021.[[70]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Modern_Family#cite_note-70) Internationally, it was released on [Disney+](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Disney+ "Disney+").[[71]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Modern_Family#cite_note-71)

## Reception

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Modern_Family&action=edit&section=20 "Edit section: Reception")]

### Ratings

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Modern_Family&action=edit&section=21 "Edit section: Ratings")]

Since its premiere, the series has remained popular. In its first season, the show became the sixth-highest rated scripted show in America and the third-highest rated new show.[[72]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Modern_Family#cite_note-tvhit1-72) Aided by winning the Primetime Emmy Award for Outstanding Comedy Series, the show's second season became the highest rated show on Wednesday during premiere week.[[73]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Modern_Family#cite_note-73) The show also rose 34% from the previous season among adults between the ages of 18 and 49.[[74]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Modern_Family#cite_note-74) The show frequently ranked as television's top scripted series in adults 18–49 as well.[[75]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Modern_Family#cite_note-75)[[76]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Modern_Family#cite_note-76)[[77]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Modern_Family#cite_note-top25-77)

The success of the show has been positively compared to _[The Cosby Show](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Cosby\_Show "The Cosby Show")_.[[78]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Modern_Family#cite_note-78) During the [2010–2011](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010%E2%80%9311_United_States_network_television_schedule "2010–11 United States network television schedule") season, _Modern Family_ was the highest rated scripted show in the 18–49 demographic, and the third-highest rated overall sitcom behind CBS's _[The Big Bang Theory](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Big\_Bang\_Theory "The Big Bang Theory")_ and _[Two and a Half Men](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Two\_and\_a\_Half\_Men "Two and a Half Men")_.[[79]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Modern_Family#cite_note-seasontwov-79)[[80]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Modern_Family#cite_note-seasontworating-80) The season also ranked first among [DVR](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Digital_video_recorder "Digital video recorder") viewers.[[81]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Modern_Family#cite_note-81)

The third-season premiere became ABC's top-rated season premiere in six years.[[82]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Modern_Family#cite_note-preliminaryratings-82) The series' success in ratings has also led it to being credited for reviving sitcoms.[[83]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Modern_Family#cite_note-83)

In 2016, a _New York Times_ study of the 50 TV shows with the most [Facebook likes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Facebook_like "Facebook like") found that _Modern Family_'s "audience pattern is the prototypical example of a city show — most popular in liberal, urban clusters in Boston, San Francisco, and Santa Barbara, California, and least popular in the more rural parts of Kentucky, Mississippi, and Arkansas".[[84]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Modern_Family#cite_note-katz20161227-84)

Following its release on streaming platforms, _Modern Family_ experienced a resurgence in popularity. Market research company Parrot Analytics, which examines consumer engagement across streaming, downloads, and social media, reported that the series has experienced a notable increase in interest since its debut on [Hulu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hulu "Hulu") and [Peacock](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peacock_(streaming_service) "Peacock (streaming service)") in 2021.[[118]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Modern_Family#cite_note-118) Streaming analytics firm FlixPatrol, which monitors daily updated VOD charts and streaming ratings across the globe, reported that it was the fifth most-streamed show on Disney+ worldwide in 2022, rising to second place in 2023 behind _[Grey's Anatomy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grey's\_Anatomy "Grey's Anatomy")_.[[119]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Modern_Family#cite_note-119) In 2024, Parrot Analytics listed _Modern Family_ among the 40 most in-demand TV shows worldwide between January 1 and August 8, noting that while most of the top ten shows appealed to viewers aged 15–31, _Modern Family_ attracted primarily Millennial and Gen X audiences (ages 32–42+).[[120]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Modern_Family#cite_note-120) In October 2024, FlixPatrol again reported _Modern Family_ as the second most-watched show on Disney+ worldwide, behind _Grey's Anatomy_.[[121]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Modern_Family#cite_note-:0-121) As of August 5, 2025, the series ranked fifth on Disney+,[[122]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Modern_Family#cite_note-122) and by early October 2025, it ranked eighth among the platform's most-viewed shows globally.[[123]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Modern_Family#cite_note-123)

[Nielsen Media Research](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nielsen_Media_Research "Nielsen Media Research"), which records streaming viewership on U.S. television screens, announced that _Modern Family_ was watched for 687 million minutes in the U.S. from August 12–18, 2024, making it the seventh most-streamed acquired series that week.[[124]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Modern_Family#cite_note-124)[[125]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Modern_Family#cite_note-125) In December 2025, Disney announced that it was among the television series to surpass one billion hours streamed on Disney+ in 2025.[[126]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Modern_Family#cite_note-126)[[127]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Modern_Family#cite_note-127) During the first half of 2026, _Modern Family_ recorded 9.77 billion minutes of watch time, ranking nineteenth among the most-streamed acquired series, according to Nielsen Media Research.[[128]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Modern_Family#cite_note-128)[[129]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Modern_Family#cite_note-129)

### Critical response

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Modern_Family&action=edit&section=22 "Edit section: Critical response")]

#### Season 1

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Modern_Family&action=edit&section=23 "Edit section: Season 1")]

The first season was met with critical acclaim. It scored 100%, based on 28 reviews, on review aggregator website [Rotten Tomatoes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rotten_Tomatoes "Rotten Tomatoes"), with an [average rating](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Weighted_arithmetic_mean "Weighted arithmetic mean") of 8.55/10 and the critical consensus: "Thanks to sharp writing and an eccentric but exceedingly likeable cast of characters, _Modern Family_ signals the triumphant return of the family comedy."[[130]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Modern_Family#cite_note-130) The first season also scored 86/100, based on 27 reviews, on review aggregator website [Metacritic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Metacritic "Metacritic"), indicating "universal acclaim".[[131]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Modern_Family#cite_note-131)

_Entertainment Weekly_ gave it an A−, calling it "immediately recognizable as the best new sitcom of the fall."[[132]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Modern_Family#cite_note-132) In _[Time](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Time\_(magazine) "Time (magazine)")_'s review, the show was named "the funniest new family comedy of the year."[[133]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Modern_Family#cite_note-133) It has also been compared to the 1970s series _[Soap](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Soap\_(TV\_series) "Soap (TV series)")_ because of the multiple-family aspect. Some have made comparisons to _[The Office](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Office\_(American\_TV\_series) "The Office (American TV series)")_ and _[Parks and Recreation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Parks\_and\_Recreation "Parks and Recreation")_ because of their mockumentary formats.[[134]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Modern_Family#cite_note-134)[BuddyTV](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BuddyTV "BuddyTV") named the show the second best show in 2009, saying, "Every actor is fantastic, every family is interesting, and unlike many shows, there isn't a weak link."[[135]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Modern_Family#cite_note-135) Robert Canning of [IGN](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IGN "IGN") gave the season an 8.9 calling it "Great" and saying "Simply put, _Modern Family_ was one of the best new comedies of the season." He also praised the ensemble cast and the characters, calling them lovable.[[136]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Modern_Family#cite_note-igns1-136) According to Metacritic, the first season was the best reviewed new broadcast television series.[[137]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Modern_Family#cite_note-137)

_Modern Family_ drew criticism from the [LGBT](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/LGBT "LGBT") community for its portrayal of Cameron and Mitchell as not being physically affectionate with each other. The criticism spawned a Facebook campaign to demand that Mitchell and Cameron be allowed to kiss. In response to the controversy, producers released a statement that a season two episode would address Mitchell's discomfort with [public displays of affection](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Public_display_of_affection "Public display of affection"). Executive producer Levitan has said that it was unfortunate that the issue had arisen, since the show's writers had always planned on such a scene "as part of the natural development of the show."[[138]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Modern_Family#cite_note-138) The episode "[The Kiss](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Kiss_(Modern_Family) "The Kiss (Modern Family)")" eventually aired with the kiss scene in the background, which drew praise from multiple critics.[[139]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Modern_Family#cite_note-139)[[140]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Modern_Family#cite_note-140)

#### Season 3

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Modern_Family&action=edit&section=25 "Edit section: Season 3")]

The third season was met with critical acclaim. On [Rotten Tomatoes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rotten_Tomatoes "Rotten Tomatoes"), season three has a rating of 92% based on 13 reviews, with an [average score](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Weighted_arithmetic_mean "Weighted arithmetic mean") of 8.33/10 and the consensus: "_Modern Family_ settles into a well-oiled groove, consistently delivering inspired farce and making it look effortless."[[152]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Modern_Family#cite_note-152)_[Slant Magazine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Slant\_Magazine "Slant Magazine")_ reviewer Peter Swanson wrote that while the first episode was "the type of wacky-location stunt that's usually reserved for the fifth or sixth season of a dying sitcom," the following episodes "have been better... but they're still uneven".[[153]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Modern_Family#cite_note-slant-153) He also criticized the writers for relying too much on "stunt episodes and celebrity cameos, like David Cross".[[153]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Modern_Family#cite_note-slant-153) He ultimately gave the season 3 out of 4 stars.[[153]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Modern_Family#cite_note-slant-153) James Parker of _The Atlantic_ said, at the beginning of the third season that "_Modern Family_ is very, very funny, almost ruthlessly so. It's a bit of a master class in pace and brevity. The writing is _[Vorsprung durch Technik](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vorsprung\_durch\_Technik "Vorsprung durch Technik")_: hectically compressed but dramatically elegant, prodigal in its zingers and snorters but austere in its construction." He found it an exception to his dislike for sitcoms that do not use a [laugh track](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Laugh_track "Laugh track").[[56]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Modern_Family#cite_note-parker-56) During the third season, _[New York Times](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_New\_York\_Times "The New York Times")_ columnist [Frank Bruni](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Frank_Bruni "Frank Bruni") argued that gay criticism of Cameron and Mitchell actually showed the progress gays have made toward social acceptance. "A decade ago," he wrote, "[gays] would have balked—and balked loudly—at how frequently Cameron in particular tips into limp-wristed, high-voiced caricature." But now, "most gay people trust that the television audience knows we're a diverse tribe, not easily pigeonholed. _Modern Family_ endows us with a sort of comic banality. It's an odd kind of progress. But it's progress nonetheless."[[154]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Modern_Family#cite_note-Bruni_blog_post-154)

#### Season 4

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Modern_Family&action=edit&section=26 "Edit section: Season 4")]

The fourth season of _Modern Family_ received positive reviews from critics. Rotten Tomatoes gives the season an approval rating of 67% based on 11 reviews, with an [average score](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Weighted_arithmetic_mean "Weighted arithmetic mean") of 7.75/10 and the consensus: "_Modern Family_ still has charm to burn and boasts a uniformly excellent cast, but the series' subversive edge has dulled".[[155]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Modern_Family#cite_note-155) Halfway through the season, Rachel Stein of _Television Without Pity_ wrote, "much as I liked the pairings and some of the dialogue, ["[New Year's Eve](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Year's_Eve_(Modern_Family) "New Year's Eve (Modern Family)")"] is just another contrived episode of _Modern Family_ we can cite when we talk later about how a different show should have won the 2013 Emmy for Best Comedy."[[156]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Modern_Family#cite_note-156) Dalene Rovenstein of _Paste Magazine_ gave the season a positive review, but said a better season was possible.[[157]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Modern_Family#cite_note-157)

#### Season 5

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Modern_Family&action=edit&section=27 "Edit section: Season 5")]

The fifth season of _Modern Family_ also received positive reviews. On Rotten Tomatoes, season five has a rating of 90% based on 10 reviews, with an [average score](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Weighted_arithmetic_mean "Weighted arithmetic mean") of 7.57/10 and the consensus: "_Modern Family_ returns to its conventional roots with grace in a fifth season that delights in providing reliable laughs and rekindles the show's trademark warmth".[[158]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Modern_Family#cite_note-158) Reviewing the season's first eight episodes, Matthew Wolfson of _[Slant Magazine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Slant\_Magazine "Slant Magazine")_ wrote that the show "appear[ed] to have finally arrived at the depressing and predictable low point toward which it [had] been trending for the past two years." He also went on to say that the show had "turned into a shrill pastiche of stereotypical characterizations and superficial banter lacking both feeling and wit", assigning it a rating of 1.5/4 stars.[[159]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Modern_Family#cite_note-159) Different writers for _[The A.V. Club](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_A.V.\_Club "The A.V. Club")_ rated, in total, a majority of the former-half episodes with a "B−" grade or less. One writer for the magazine, Joshua Alston, gave "[ClosetCon '13](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ClosetCon_'13 "ClosetCon '13")" a "C+" and remarked that "_Modern Family_ becomes a high-wire act when it separates its characters into three storylines with no overlap between them."[[160]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Modern_Family#cite_note-160) The second half was more warmly received, with three episodes rated an "A−" or higher.

The show's sixth season received highly positive reviews from TV critics, with some claiming that it was an improvement over the last few seasons.[[161]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Modern_Family#cite_note-fourthmic.com-161) This season has a rating of 100% on [Rotten Tomatoes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rotten_Tomatoes "Rotten Tomatoes") based on 7 reviews, with an [average score](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Weighted_arithmetic_mean "Weighted arithmetic mean") of 7.67/10.[[162]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Modern_Family#cite_note-162) Joshua Alston and Gwen Ihnat of _[The A.V. You'll Love It!" – marking an improvement over the repeated "C" grade given throughout the previous season's former half.[[163]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Modern_Family#cite_note-163) "Connection Lost" received high critical acclaim, with many praising the episode's writing, originality and "success in transcending what could have been a gimicky episode".[[164]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Modern_Family#cite_note-164)[[165]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Modern_Family#cite_note-165)[[166]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Modern_Family#cite_note-166) In her review for "Closet? You'll Love It!" Gwen Ihnat of _The A.V. Club_ stated that the episode represents "all the reasons why we still watch _Modern Family_" and awarded the episode an A−.[[167]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Modern_Family#cite_note-167) On the same site, David Kallison reviewed "Grill, Interrupted", saying: "This season proves that sitcoms can survive on solid characters and solid jokes."[[168]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Modern_Family#cite_note-168)

The seventh season received positive reviews from critics with many critics calling it similar to the fourth and fifth seasons. On Rotten Tomatoes, this season is rated 67% with 6 reviews and an average rating of 6.5/10.[[169]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Modern_Family#cite_note-169) Kyle Fowle from _[The A.V. #### Later seasons

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Modern_Family&action=edit&section=30 "Edit section: Later seasons")]

The series was renewed for a 9th and 10th season on May 10, 2017.[[172]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Modern_Family#cite_note-Goldberg-172) Season 9 premiered on September 27, 2017, while season 10 premiered on September 26, 2018.[[173]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Modern_Family#cite_note-173)

Seasons 8 and 9 received mixed-to-positive reviews from critics, with main criticisms directed at the lack of character development, overstuffing of episodes, and too many [filler episodes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Filler_episode "Filler episode") per season. While the show continued to be praised for its charm, witty writing, and the cast's performances, criticism grew in these seasons, particularly from reviewers such as those at _[The A.V. Club](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_A.V.\_Club "The A.V. Club")_.

In January 2018, Christopher Lloyd and Steve Levitan announced that season 10 would most likely be the final season, during the [Television Critics Association](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Television_Critics_Association "Television Critics Association")'s winter press tour.[[174]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Modern_Family#cite_note-174) However, in August 2018, reports indicated that ABC was in discussions to renew the series for a potential eleventh season.[[175]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Modern_Family#cite_note-175)

Season 10 received positive reviews from critics, citing the season as a significant improvement over the last two. The series was praised for its tackling of Haley's pregnancy, the humor of Mitch and Cam looking after Cal, and its dealing with change in a positive way. Episodes "Torn Between Two Lovers", "Good Grief", and "A Year Of Birthdays" were particularly praised.

The series was renewed for an eleventh season on January 7, 2019, which was confirmed as the final season on February 5. The last season premiered on September 25, 2019, and aired its last episode on April 8, 2020.[[176]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Modern_Family#cite_note-176)[[177]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Modern_Family#cite_note-Ausiello-177)[[178]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Modern_Family#cite_note-September_25,_2019-178)

Season 11 similarly received positive reviews. The season was praised for its themes of change and ending, and the improved humor upon the last seasons, with particular attention to episodes "The Prescott", "Legacy", "Spuds" and "Finale".

Every season of the show was also named one of the top 10 TV seasons of the year (from 2009 to 2012) by the [American Film Institute](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Film_Institute "American Film Institute").[[187]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Modern_Family#cite_note-187)
